skincare-packaging-series-analysis.title: Skincare Packaging: Build One System Across Different Products
skincare-packaging-series-analysis.summary: Coordinate skincare cartons and gift sets across different containers with clear SKU hierarchy, shared material references and sample checks.
skincare-packaging-series-analysis.intro: Build a skincare packaging range around a clear product-name hierarchy and shared production references, while allowing different structures for different containers. Group SKUs by size and use before assuming they can share tooling. Test the smallest format for readability and the full gift set for removal. Colour should help identify products without being the only distinction.
sections: Published reference

Xaime Betancur’s Belle Girl case describes a skincare identity extending across bottles, tubes, jars and secondary boxes. Repeated typography, restrained colour and gold accents connect the formats. The published design is credited to its creator; no MTT production relationship is implied. Read the Xaime Betancur: Belle Girl.
The buyer’s challenge

A skincare range needs family resemblance without making customers confuse a cleanser with a serum. Establish a fixed brand position and product-name hierarchy, then use a limited variable element to distinguish each item. Do not depend on colour alone.
Structure and material direction: our analysis

Group products by container size before choosing carton formats. Shared paper and print specifications may be practical even when the cutting dies differ. For a gift set, arrange the products in their intended use order and leave access around pumps and lids. Do not use a decorative insert as evidence of leak containment.
What to check in sampling

Review the smallest carton as well as the largest: text that fits one may fail on another. Compare printed samples across the range, check barcode placement with the buyer and confirm all required product information before artwork approval.
Separate shared references from shared tools

Two SKUs can share a paper and colour target without sharing a cutting die. A larger carton may need a different panel layout, while a different product name may require separate artwork. Record common references and unique components in a SKU table so a lower total tooling estimate is not assumed from visual similarity.
Prepare a comparable quotation

Send a SKU table with container measurements, quantities, languages and artwork versions. Request costs by SKU and identify which print, foil and cutting tools can actually be shared. Prepare the SKU and quotation brief.

jewelry-packaging-repeat-use-analysis.title: Jewelry Boxes: Design the Interior for Repeated Handling
jewelry-packaging-repeat-use-analysis.summary: Review ring slots, necklace routing, lining and repeated handling before approving jewelry presentation packaging.
jewelry-packaging-repeat-use-analysis.intro: Choose jewelry-box interiors around the way each piece is held and removed. Ring slots, pendant supports and necklace routing are different tasks. Evaluate the final lining with representative sizes and repeated handling, checking edges and polished surfaces. A luxurious fabric does not by itself establish retention, durability or tarnish protection for the jewelry inside.
sections: Published reference

Alejandra Frakes documents jewelry and watch presentation packaging for Chippenhook, including wrapped board and lined interiors. The portfolio highlights repeat handling and product-specific interior geometry. These are third-party examples, not MTT delivery claims. Read the Alejandra Frakes: Jewelry & Presentation Packaging.
The buyer’s challenge

A ring, pendant and necklace need different retention. A universal foam opening may display one item well while allowing another to shift. Decide how the piece is presented, how staff remove it and whether the package is also intended for travel.
Structure and material direction: our analysis

For a ring, review the slot grip with representative shank sizes. For a necklace, consider attachment points, chain routing and space behind the display pad. A fabric-covered insert changes the final cavity dimensions; confirm the assembled lining rather than only the bare foam shape.
What to check in sampling

Agree a repeated-opening check with the supplier and inspect lining edges, loose fibres, hinge behaviour and contact with polished surfaces. Do not infer durability or tarnish protection from a luxurious fabric appearance. Material compatibility needs review with the actual jewelry finish.
Test the smallest piece as well as the largest

A slot that holds the widest ring shank may release a narrower one. A chain route that suits a short pendant can leave a longer chain loose behind the pad. Identify the approved size range, then inspect removal, snagging and return to position with the final lined insert.
Prepare a comparable quotation

Provide the jewelry range, size variation, intended retail handling, preferred lining and quantity by format. Request a sample with the final lining and attachment method, not just a colour swatch. Compare insert constructions.

tea-gift-box-drawer-analysis.title: Tea Gift Boxes: Use the Opening Sequence to Organize Choice
tea-gift-box-drawer-analysis.summary: Plan tea gift drawers around sealed packs, removal access, ribbon pulls and assortment information before approving decoration.
tea-gift-box-drawer-analysis.intro: A tea drawer gift box should make the assortment easy to identify and remove without disturbing neighbouring packs. Plan the tin or sachet layout, ribbon pull and information card together. Check loaded drawer travel after wrapping. The gift box organizes presentation; the tea’s primary packaging must separately meet its freshness and contact requirements.
sections: Published reference

Pentagram’s Teabox project uses a coordinated identity, a colour system and slide-open packaging. Its published description also discusses tactile printed finishes. The useful reference is the relationship between navigation and presentation, rather than a template to copy. Read the Pentagram: Teabox.
The buyer’s challenge

A tea assortment should help the recipient understand what is inside before removing every packet. Organize the range with clear names and an intentional sequence. The presentation box and the tea’s sealed primary pack have separate jobs.
Structure and material direction: our analysis

Compare a drawer format with a divided lift-off box. Check that packets or tins can be removed without pulling neighbouring items out. Keep drawer friction practical after wrapping, and specify whether the ribbon is a functional pull or a decorative bow. Leave room for the brewing information card if one is required.
What to check in sampling

Review odour, storage and barrier requirements with the primary-pack supplier; a decorative rigid box alone is not a freshness system. Check packet fit, drawer travel and label legibility on the assembled sample. Avoid adding finishes that obscure variant information.
Reserve space for the card without changing the fit

Place the brewing card above or beside the sealed packs only after checking drawer travel. A loose card can catch at the sleeve mouth; a thick folded leaflet can change the loaded height. We would locate it deliberately and trial opening after the full set has been packed.
Prepare a comparable quotation
List every tea pack size, assortment quantity, primary-pack format and information insert. Ask for the gift box and inner components as separate quotation items. Compare opening structures.

electronics-paperboard-insert-analysis.title: Small Electronics: Separate Product Support from Accessory Storage
electronics-paperboard-insert-analysis.summary: Separate devices, cables and booklets in a paperboard insert while reviewing sensitive surfaces, removal and complete-pack testing.
electronics-paperboard-insert-analysis.intro: For a small electronics kit, allocate product support and accessory storage separately before setting box depth. Keep pressure away from connectors, buttons and sensitive surfaces, and restrain cables so they cannot move onto the device. Compare the complete loaded layout. A decorative paperboard insert should not be assumed to meet device-specific electrostatic or transport requirements.
sections: Published reference

Metsä Board presents paperboard applications for consumer-electronics retail and e-commerce packaging. The reference supports considering paperboard as a packaging direction; it does not validate a particular device, insert geometry or transport test. Read the Metsä Board: Consumer electronics packaging.
The buyer’s challenge

A compact device, cable and booklet can make a box unnecessarily deep if they are stacked without a plan. Start with the product’s vulnerable areas and removal path, then allocate the accessories to a deliberate compartment.
Structure and material direction: our analysis

A folded platform can locate the device while a separate pocket stores the cable. Compare this with a molded insert when the shape is complex. Keep connectors, buttons and delicate surfaces away from concentrated pressure. Decorative papers should not be assumed to provide electrostatic protection.
What to check in sampling

Build a complete pack-out sample using the actual device, accessories and instructions. Check movement, cable restraint, removal access and repeated packing. Confirm any device-specific handling and transport requirements with the buyer before selecting a test plan.
Compare side storage with under-tray storage

A side pocket increases footprint but can make accessories visible immediately. Under-tray storage can keep the footprint compact, but adds depth and another removal step. Compare both with the actual cable bend and booklet thickness before choosing the external size.
Prepare a comparable quotation

Send product dimensions and weight, accessory list, sensitive surfaces, shipping channel and quantity. Ask the quotation to identify the outer package, insert, accessory compartment and shipping protection separately. Review insert selection.

window-carton-presentation-analysis.title: Window Cartons: Balance Product Visibility and Box Support
window-carton-presentation-analysis.summary: Review window size, film attachment, remaining carton frame and product restraint before approving a retail carton.
window-carton-presentation-analysis.intro: A carton window should reveal the detail a customer needs to see while leaving enough structure around it. Decide whether the opening is covered, then review folds, film attachment and product restraint together. A large cut-out may look attractive but weaken handling. Validate the assembled carton with its contents before approving the window artwork.
sections: Published reference

Metsä Board’s bakery packaging case presents a windowed carton application. It is a useful reference for the relationship between display and a paperboard structure. The illustrated example on this page is an independent carton concept, not a reproduction of that project. Read the Metsä Board: Case bakery packaging.
The buyer’s challenge

A larger window reveals more product but removes material from the panel. Choose what the customer needs to see, then review the remaining frame, folds and closure. A window should have a functional reason rather than simply filling the largest possible area.
Structure and material direction: our analysis

Compare an open cut-out with a covered window according to the product and handling route. Define the intended window position and any film attachment before artwork approval. Keep graphics and essential information away from the cut edge. A presentation carton does not automatically provide a moisture or grease barrier.
What to check in sampling

Inspect the assembled sample for distortion, window adhesion where applicable and product movement. For food use, obtain suitability documentation for the actual board, inks, adhesives and direct-contact components; visual similarity to another pack is not evidence of suitability.
Check the pack from the shelf distance

Choose the visible product feature first, then check whether it remains in the opening when the pack is handled. If the product rotates, a larger window may not solve the problem; the internal support needs attention. Keep the remaining frame clear of a fold that already carries handling load.
Prepare a comparable quotation

Provide product dimensions, contact conditions, shelf or delivery use, quantity and preferred viewing area. Ask the supplier to identify window material and assembly charges separately. Compare packaging families.

collectors-packaging-story-material-anal.title: Collector Packaging: Let Material Support the Story
collectors-packaging-story-material-anal.summary: Choose collector packaging materials around an authorised story, documented sourcing and repeatable finishing.
collectors-packaging-story-material-anal.intro: For collector packaging, choose materials that support an authorised product story and remain practical to source and finish. Confirm evidence before describing a special provenance. Test the finest decoration on the actual paper, then check retention separately. An expensive finish adds little if it obscures the message or cannot be repeated consistently for the order.
sections: Published reference

Avery Dennison’s Pentawards feature describes Lost Barrels by Meyer-Näkel and the design by Ruska Martín. Its account links the packaging material and visual details to the product story. This is third-party editorial reference material, not an MTT client case. Read the Avery Dennison M_use: Pentawards 2024.
The buyer’s challenge

A collector pack needs a reason for its materials beyond expense. Identify the detail the buyer should notice first and explain how it relates to the product. Do not invent a provenance story or use material claims that cannot be documented.
Structure and material direction: our analysis

For a paper-based presentation direction, compare a textured wrap with a restrained foil detail rather than adding multiple competing finishes. If a customer requests reclaimed or specially sourced material, review consistency, availability and evidence before committing. A substitute paper cannot be described as the original material.
What to check in sampling

Approve the paper, foil and colour together. Check the finest artwork details, edge wrapping and resistance to ordinary handling. A decorative sample should be accompanied by a separate assessment of how the product is retained and shipped.
Plan for a material replacement before it is needed

If a special stock becomes unavailable, decide which features can change and which claims must be removed. A similar colour can preserve a visual reference without preserving provenance. Retain an approved fallback sample and separate its description from the original material story.
Prepare a comparable quotation

Supply the brand story, authorised assets, required material claims, product dimensions and quantity. Separate decorative setup costs from the structural package and transport packing in the quote. Review finishing proofs.

modular-perfume-packaging-analysis.title: Personalized Perfume Sets: Plan the Insert Around Every Combination
modular-perfume-packaging-analysis.summary: Plan shared perfume gift boxes and variant inserts around a configuration matrix, fit checks and packing instructions.
modular-perfume-packaging-analysis.intro: A personalised perfume set needs an approved configuration list before a shared insert can be chosen. Compare the smallest, largest and differently shaped assemblies, including caps and accessories. A common outer box with variant inserts may be practical, but it adds packing and stock-control work. Test each distinct support condition rather than extrapolating from one attractive arrangement.
sections: Published reference

The same Avery Dennison feature identifies EDIT (036), by Lavernia & Cienfuegos, as a perfume personalization concept with interchangeable components. It is explicitly a concept reference. No production result or MTT involvement is claimed here. Read the Avery Dennison M_use: EDIT (036) concept.
The buyer’s challenge

Personalization increases the number of combinations an insert may need to hold. A cavity developed around one bottle assembly can fail when the stopper, base or accessory changes. Define the allowed configurations before choosing a common box.
Structure and material direction: our analysis

Create a dimensional envelope for each assembly and compare a shared outer box with variant-specific inserts. A removable insert component may be worth evaluating, but it adds packing instructions and inventory. Keep the customer’s selection visible in the SKU or pack-out documentation.
What to check in sampling

Sample the smallest and largest approved configurations and any shape that introduces a new contact point. Review clearance, movement and removal. A render of one configuration cannot demonstrate that all combinations fit. Do not label a pack universal until its approved scope is documented.
Use a configuration matrix at pack-out

• Configuration code and fitted cap or base.
  • Maximum assembled dimensions and filled weight.
  • Compatible insert revision.
  • Accessories and label version.
  • Physical fit check status.
Include shape changes as well as size extremes: the tallest version is not necessarily the hardest to support.
Prepare a comparable quotation

Provide a configuration matrix, assembly dimensions, filled weights, quantity by option and accessory list. Request the common outer box and each insert variant as separate items so the effect of personalization is visible. Review bottle support and clearance.

custom-box-structure-guide.title: Custom Box Structures: Lift-Off, Magnetic, Drawer or Carton?
custom-box-structure-guide.summary: Compare custom box opening styles for perfume, skincare and gift sets. Separate rigid, folding and corrugated structures before choosing materials and artwork.
custom-box-structure-guide.intro: Choose the box opening around loading, customer access and the intended presentation. A lift-off lid, magnetic cover and sliding drawer require different clearances and handling space. Separate wrapped rigid structures from paperboard cartons and corrugated mailers. Shortlist two workable openings before choosing decoration, then compare both with the actual contents and packing method.
faq: Is a magnetic box always more luxurious than a lift-off box?
No. Material feel, finish execution, fit and the intended opening experience matter. Compare physical samples for the same product rather than ranking quality by the closure alone.
Can a rigid box ship flat?

Some purpose-designed collapsible rigid boxes can fold flat. A conventional assembled lift-off box does not. Confirm the actual supplied configuration and the assembly required at your packing location.
Does a hinged lid make a mailer a rigid gift box?
No. A corrugated mailer uses fluted board and folded locking parts. A wrapped rigid book box uses a different board and assembly method even though both can open from the rear.
sections: Start with the product, not the decoration

Write down the assembled product dimensions, filled weight, number of pieces, sales channel and intended opening sequence. Distinguish internal box size from the outer size used to plan a bag or shipper. A screen image is useful for visual direction, but does not establish dimensions or closing clearances. Select the structure first so that artwork follows the real panels and seams.
Lift-off versus magnetic: what changes for a bottle?

A lift-off rigid box has a separate cap and base. It exposes the contents when the cap is removed, but the user needs somewhere to put the lid. A magnetic book box keeps its lid attached at the spine and needs room for that lid to swing. Both require a bottle support and clearance over the cap. Choose the handling experience before choosing the finish. Compare the single-bottle lift-off design with the hinged skincare set layout; the latter illustrates a different product arrangement, not an interchangeable bottle insert.
Drawer, hexagonal and pillow are different structural decisions

A drawer tray moves inside a sleeve: review the pull attachment and product retention while it slides. A hexagonal lift-off box has matching six-sided components and needs a deliberate internal layout. A pillow carton closes at curved ends and offers a different usable volume from a rectangular tray. Compare the coffee drawer, hexagonal sweets box and pillow carton. These are selection references, not proof of a tested load or finished order.
Keep the packaging families clear

Wrapped rigid board is one construction family; creased paperboard cartons and fluted corrugated packs are others. A corrugated mailer may also have a rear-hinged lid, but its folded walls and side wings are not the same construction as a wrapped magnetic book box. Use the family comparison to separate presentation and transport requirements. The FEFCO design catalogue provides a common naming reference for corrugated styles; a style code does not specify board performance.
Approve opening and removal before print production

Load the sample with the actual contents. Remove the lid, slide the drawer or open the flap repeatedly as the customer would. Check the tall parts of the product, finger access, seam alignment and any ribbon pull. Then review artwork at the folds and wrap joins. Avoid assigning one clearance to every design: material thickness, dimensions and construction affect the fit.
Send two options for a useful comparison

Shortlist two structures with the same contents and quantity. Ask for the board, wrap, insert, print, finishes, setup charges and shipping scope to be identified separately. A comparison with different inserts or delivery terms is not a like-for-like price comparison. Use Design Your Box to record an initial visual direction if useful.

printing-finishing-guide.title: Matte, Gloss, Foil or Spot UV: Custom Packaging Finishes
printing-finishing-guide.summary: Compare matte and gloss surfaces, foil, embossing and spot UV for custom packaging. Learn what to specify and check on the actual paper sample.
printing-finishing-guide.intro: Choose the finish around the visual or tactile detail you want buyers to notice, then test it on the intended paper. Matte, gloss, foil and spot effects respond differently to substrate and artwork. Review small details, joins and handling marks before combining processes. A screen mock-up cannot establish registration, adhesion or the final surface appearance.
faq: Can I combine foil, embossing and spot UV?
A combination may be feasible, but the substrate, operation sequence, detail and registration need review. Specify the intended areas and ask for a sample before committing to production.
Will a gloss finish make any material look the same?
No. The base material, printed coverage and coating or lamination route affect appearance. Compare the actual materials.
Does more finishing always mean better packaging?
No. Choose effects that support the design and remain clear in production. Several competing effects can make the hierarchy less readable and add setup costs.
sections: Matte versus gloss: start with the broad surface

A matte surface gives a less reflective appearance; a gloss surface emphasizes reflections and printed colour. Coatings and film laminations are different specifications and should not be treated as interchangeable. Compare the gloss perfume design with the matte collagen set as visual directions, then approve physical paper samples. A screen cannot reproduce surface feel.
Foil adds a surface effect, not an opening structure

Foil can highlight a logo or outline, but the result depends on the foil, paper, tooling and production route. Keep delicate detail away from difficult wrap corners and discuss the artwork with the converter. The hexagonal gift design combines dyed paper and gold foil outlines. The cloth-wrapped ring design needs its own foil trial because cloth texture differs from smooth paper.
Emboss and deboss change surface relief

Embossing raises a feature; debossing presses it into the surface. Artwork, tooling, material thickness and assembly sequence affect the result. Ask how the effect is made in the chosen build and whether it affects the reverse surface. A border on the textured skincare wrap should be evaluated on that material rather than copied from a smooth-paper proof.
Spot UV needs a defined area and a compatibility check

Selective gloss UV can contrast with a matte background. Supply a separate mask for the intended area and agree alignment requirements with production. Review adhesion, cure, fold behaviour and the visual result on the selected surface. Do not assume the same gloss on absorbent uncoated stock and coated paper. The collagen set is a reference for this surface contrast.
Match a set with physical references

A rigid-box wrap, bag paper and greeting card can show the same ink differently. Decide whether the priority is the closest colour match, the same texture or a deliberate contrast. Compare the assembled set under consistent lighting and retain the approved reference. Review ribbons and foil alongside the printed paper rather than choosing each from unrelated screen images.
Prepare artwork and quote each operation

Identify ordinary print, foil, UV and relief areas separately. Keep key information away from cuts, folds and wrap joins using the allowances agreed for that structure; there is no single safe-zone value for all packaging. Ask for each setup or tooling charge and sample scope. Send your artwork and preferred finish, using the brief checklist if the specification is still open.

custom-inserts-product-protection.title: Paperboard vs Molded Pulp vs EVA: Choosing Custom Inserts
custom-inserts-product-protection.summary: Choose a custom insert around product geometry, removal access and packaging use. Compare paperboard, molded pulp, EVA and fabric-covered support.
custom-inserts-product-protection.intro: Choose a custom insert by the product’s support needs, packing method and acceptable contact, then compare material routes. A folded platform, molded support and foam cavity can solve different problems. Test the final assembled insert, including any covering. Material names and visual neatness alone cannot establish retention or protection across the intended product range.
faq: Is EVA always the safest insert for glass?
No material name establishes protection on its own. Geometry, support, material properties and the complete shipping pack need a loaded-sample review and appropriate testing.
Can one insert hold a whole gift set?
Yes, if each item has suitable support and removal access. Include every item, leaflet and accessory when defining the available space.
Is a paper insert automatically recyclable?
Do not assume that. Review coatings, adhesives, combined materials, separation and the actual collection route in the destination market.
sections: Measure the assembled product and identify contact areas

Provide dimensions with caps, pumps and decorations fitted, plus filled weight and photographs from several sides. Mark surfaces that should not be rubbed or loaded. Define whether the product lies down or stands up. A jar and two bottles, as in the skincare set, need separate positions and a review of lid clearance. Do not size a cavity from a photograph or nominal bottle capacity.
Paperboard: folded support with deliberate contact points

Folded or die-cut paperboard can create platforms, dividers and locating features. Specify where the product rests and how it is restrained; an attractive empty cutout does not prove support. Review creases, assembly and loaded deformation on the sample. Check the full material combination and local collection route before making recyclability claims. The carton example uses paperboard support, with grade and fit still to be confirmed.
Molded pulp: formed geometry and a tooling decision

Molded-fibre inserts can form three-dimensional support around a product. Surface appearance and dimensional behaviour depend on the process and material. Confirm the tooling scope, sample method and product contact areas before selecting it for appearance alone. Read the molded-pulp guide for cosmetics alongside your actual product requirements.
EVA and covered support: specify the full build

Cut foam can form locating cavities, but foam type, density, thickness and the remaining material between cavities need review. A fabric cover changes the contact surface and usable fit. Check for rubbing, lint, adhesive visibility and removal force. In the ring keepsake layout, the fabric-lined slit must suit the ring and its setting; the lining is not automatically an anti-tarnish material.
Access can matter as much as a tight fit

Allow a practical grip, finger recess or secured lift ribbon. A cavity that holds an item but makes removal awkward is not finished engineering. For a drawer, check stability during sliding; for a hinged lid, check the closing sweep; for a lift-off lid, check the full height under the cap. Use the opening guide to coordinate the insert and box.
Validate the full pack and record the approved version

Use actual contents to check loading, removal, closure and the intended handling sequence. Confirm the transport test scope for the complete pack separately. Record material, cavity drawing, product revision and approved sample together. If the bottle or cap changes, review the fit again. Send the product data for an insert review; include quantity, destination and any direct-contact requirements.

rigid-box-vs-folding-carton.title: Rigid Box vs Folding Carton vs Corrugated: How to Choose
rigid-box-vs-folding-carton.summary: Compare rigid boxes, folding cartons and corrugated packaging by presentation, packing, material use and shipping needs, with practical product examples.
rigid-box-vs-folding-carton.intro: Choose rigid, folding-carton or corrugated packaging by the job each layer must perform. A presentation shell, retail carton and transport pack are not interchangeable even when their lids look similar. Compare packing labour, complete cost and product support as well as appearance. Some projects need a combination; some rigid designs can also be supplied folded.
faq: Are all rigid boxes unable to fold flat?
No. Collapsible rigid structures exist. Specify whether your chosen design is supplied assembled or flat, and include assembly work when comparing costs.
Does a folding carton need an outer shipping pack?
That depends on the product and distribution route. Do not assume a retail carton alone is adequate for parcel shipping; review the full loaded system.
Which family is the cheapest?
There is no dependable universal ranking for every project. Compare quotes with the same contents, quantities, finishes, packing and delivery scope.
sections: Three families, three different starting points

• Rigid box: structural board is wrapped or otherwise finished and assembled into a firm presentation format. Some designs are collapsible; many are supplied erected.
  • Folding carton: creased paperboard forms panels, end flaps and glued or locking features. Supply and erection methods depend on the design.
  • Corrugated packaging: fluted material between liners forms shipping cartons, mailers or other structures. Board grade, joints, supports and the route must be reviewed together.
Paper thickness alone is not a complete performance specification.
Choose by what the customer must do

A gift recipient may keep a rigid box; a retail customer may open a carton once; a fulfilment team needs a pack that can be assembled and sealed consistently. Start with those tasks. A magnetic skincare set presents several items together. A crash-lock skincare carton provides a different retail packing route. A four-flap corrugated carton can serve an outer transport role. They are not interchangeable specifications.
Compare total scope, not a presumed cheapest family

Request a quote for the same product count, quantity and delivery scope. Separate board and wrap, insert, printing, finishing, tooling, assembly and packing. Also ask for sample charges and freight. Do not assume a universal quantity at which one family becomes cheaper: size, production route, print coverage and setup all matter. Obtain packed carton dimensions if empty packaging must travel to your filling site.
Premium appearance is not limited to one board family

A folding carton can use precise typography, bright printing and an appropriate finish. A rigid box can be restrained or colourful. Neither a magnet nor a drawer is sufficient to define quality, and similar opening actions can be engineered in different materials. Evaluate the actual construction and sample rather than relying only on names such as “luxury” or “premium”.
Separate the display box from shipping protection

For a perfume order, compare a presentation box with a corrugated mailer. If one sits inside the other, size the outer pack from the finished packed presentation box. Agree product restraint, sealing and an appropriate testing plan. A beautiful box, a flute designation or a style drawing does not establish that the full pack will survive the distribution route.
A short selection checklist

• What is the complete product envelope and loaded weight?
  • Is the pack for display, carrying, delivery or several of these?
  • Will it arrive at the filling site flat or erected?
  • Who assembles, loads and seals it?
  • Are inserts, cards and a bag part of the order?
  • Which physical sample and transport checks need approval?
Request a comparison using the same brief. For opening details, read the box structure guide.

how-to-write-a-packaging-brief.title: Custom Packaging Brief Checklist: What to Send for a Quote
how-to-write-a-packaging-brief.summary: Prepare a packaging brief with dimensions, quantity, materials, artwork, inserts and delivery scope. Includes a copyable checklist for boxes, bags and gift sets.
how-to-write-a-packaging-brief.intro: A useful packaging brief identifies the contents, dimensions, intended use, quantity and approval requirements before listing finishes. Mark provisional decisions rather than asking suppliers to guess. Separate the box, insert, accessories and delivery scope so quotations can be compared. Keep the approved brief linked to the drawing and sample revisions as the project develops.
faq: Can I ask for a quote before I know the material?
Yes. Share the product, quantity, opening preference and delivery needs, and mark the material undecided. A final price still needs an agreed specification.
Can a reference image replace dimensions?
No. It communicates appearance and opening direction, but it does not establish the actual product envelope or manufacturing dimensions.
Should bags and ribbons use the same order quantity as boxes?
State quantities separately. Extra bags, multiple ribbon lengths or different artwork versions may change the required quantities and quote.
sections: Describe the product as it will be packed

Measure the actual assembled product, including caps and projecting parts, and provide its loaded weight. List the number of pieces in each set. For food already sealed in a tray or pouch, measure that sealed pack rather than the loose contents. For example, the macaron window carton must accommodate the tray rim and cover as well as the food.
Use the right dimension convention

State finished internal box dimensions as length × width × height, and label product dimensions separately. A shopping bag uses width × side gusset × height and should be sized from the finished outer box with an agreed loading orientation. Do not reuse the bottle dimensions as bag dimensions. Identify the unit of measurement and mark all provisional dimensions.
Copy this enquiry checklist

• Product name and current development stage:
  • Assembled product dimensions, units and loaded weight:
  • Items per set and individual sizes:
  • Packaging role: retail / gifting / parcel delivery:
  • Preferred structure or two options to compare:
  • Material and finish preferences, or undecided:
  • Insert, bag, card, ribbon and tissue requirements:
  • Quantity by size, artwork version and accessory:
  • Artwork files and separate foil / UV / emboss artwork, if ready:
  • Destination, target arrival date and delivery terms to discuss:
  • Optional budget range and currency:
  • Sample, tooling and testing requirements:
Mark missing items “to be confirmed” instead of guessing.
Ask for an itemized commercial scope

Separate the box, insert and accessories, and ask which print and finishing operations are included. Request sample and tooling costs separately, plus freight and any tax or duty assumptions. State whether packing takes place at your facility or elsewhere. A price for an empty box and a price for a packed gift set cover different work. Use the coffee set to consider whether tasting cards are supplied loose or placed in the box.
Food and sensitive product details need their own review

State whether packaging touches the food directly, the storage conditions and the destination. A general “food grade” label is not enough to determine suitability for a particular use. The FDA explains how food-contact component status is assessed for the United States; other destinations need their own review. This guide does not certify any catalogue pack.
Keep one current specification and a clear approval path

Attach the current artwork revision and identify who approves structure, colour and the physical sample. Do not approve print files while the structure is still changing. Start with the box planning tool if a visual draft helps, or send the checklist directly. Neither an account nor a completed tool design is required to enquire.
